Key
  • Each panel is a board state (node). Columns left to right: s/w (stock count on top, waste below), the tableau columns (a count of face-down cards on top when there are any), and one home pile per suit (top card only). Piles stack downward.
  • Node ID above each panel: [fork]-[play]. Fork 01 is the leftmost column; play 000 is the deal.
  • Each play flows down to the next node: a white glow marks the card(s) picked up, a gold glow marks where they are put down, and a gold connector joins them.
  • Connectors show the degree of a progressive play, judged from the plays available at that moment: solid gold is first degree (p¹, the direct path); two, three or four short dashes in the middle mark p², p³, p⁴. A dashed grey line will mark a truly regressive play.
  • When a node has more than one available play, the tree forks to the right: a darker copy of the node, labelled with the origin node ID plus .f1, .f2, …, joined by a horizontal line. The fork's first play leaves from the copy.
  • Below each final node: the full game ID, ending in its result (W/L and number of plays).
